I've been working this land for over 30 years. My husband helps when he can, but mostly it's me and sometimes my son comes back from the city during harvest. We have about 10 mu of flat land here in Quzhou. Everyone around here grows winter wheat and summer maize — that's what this land is suited for, that's what the market buys, that's what I know how to grow. I'm not going to try cotton or vegetables at my age. Too much risk, too much unfamiliar work.

For wheat, I already planted it last October. I'll put on urea at jointing stage and again at heading. I'll irrigate three times — once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at anthesis. Water is expensive now with the well pumping fees, but wheat needs it. I'll spray herbicide early spring and a fungicide before heading because rust and powdery mildew are bad some years here.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll plant maize right away — no time to waste, we want it in the ground quickly to get the full growing days before frost. I'll direct-seed without ploughing to save time and cost. One irrigation if August is dry. Spray for corn borer and armyworm.

I use the improved wheat variety from the township seed station — it yields well and everyone here uses it. For maize I always buy hybrid seed, you can't use saved seed for maize, the dealers say, and the yields really are better.

My fertilizer practice is what my father-in-law taught me and what the village technician told us years ago. Maybe I use a bit more nitrogen than I should, but I'd rather not risk a poor harvest.
